title: Gwalior Truck Crash Near Temple Kills 14 Devotees, Families Allege Delayed Rescue
excerpt: A paddy-laden truck broke through barricades on a restricted slope and ran over pilgrims near Sheetla Mata Temple at 1:30 a.m.; the collector confirmed the toll had risen to 14 after police first reported 12 dead.
body:
• At least 14 devotees were killed near the Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior, according to the district collector on Sunday, after earlier police counts put the toll at 12 — figures rose as more of the injured died or were confirmed.
  • A paddy-laden truck lost control at about 1:30 a.m. on a steep, restricted road from Chhinor, broke through police barricades and ran over pilgrims before hitting the temple gate and wall.
  • Thirty-nine people were taken to hospital, including two injured police personnel; five to six were critically injured with fractures, officials said.
  • Madhya Pradesh announced Rs 4 lakh for each bereaved family, Rs 2 lakh for the seriously injured and Rs 50,000 for other injured, with free treatment.

At least 14 people were killed after a paddy-laden truck ran over devotees near the Sheetla Mata Temple in Gwalior early on Sunday, according to district officials, in one of the deadliest accidents of this Navratri season. The toll has moved as officials confirmed cases in hospital: Gwalior Senior Superintendent of Police Dharmveer Singh first said 12 of 39 people taken to hospital had died, according to NDTV and ANI via LatestLY, and Collector Ruchika Chauhan later confirmed on Sunday that it had risen to 14, ANI reported.

The accident occurred at about 1:30 a.m. as large numbers of pilgrims were travelling to the temple. The truck, coming from the Chhinor direction, lost control on a steep slope where heavy vehicles are restricted, officials said.

How the truck reached the crowd

"Around 1.30 AM, a truck loaded with paddy was stopped there. It broke through the police barricades, suddenly lost control, came down, and crashed into the outer wall and gate of the temple. The devotees who were on the road were crushed underneath it."

https://x.com/PTI_News/status/2111681688812277951 — Dharmveer Singh, Gwalior Senior Superintendent of Police

Two police personnel on duty at the spot were also injured. Of those taken to hospital, five to six patients were critically injured with fractures and the rest sustained minor injuries, Singh said. An eyewitness whose brother was injured said the truck appeared overloaded and came suddenly, running over shops and people on the road.

Collector Chauhan said a stopper and a police checkpoint were present on the road during Navratri, and how the vehicle managed to get through is under investigation. An RTO team has been sent to inspect the truck mechanically to establish what went wrong and why it veered continuously to the left.

Anger over rescue and communication

At the hospital and postmortem centre on Sunday, grieving families alleged police negligence and delays in rescue and in informing relatives. Some told ANI they learned of a death through friends rather than officials, and a woman whose daughter was missing accused police of preventing the family from searching. Those allegations, reported by ANI, have not been answered in detail by the district administration in the reports available so far.

Compensation and next steps

Chief Minister Mohan Yadav announced Rs 4 lakh for the family of each person killed, Rs 2 lakh for each seriously injured person and Rs 50,000 for each other injured person, with free treatment for all the injured. He said the affected families are from Gwalior, Shivpuri and Sheopur, and directed two ministers to reach Gwalior. Investigators now face two linked questions: the mechanical condition and loading of the truck, and the failure of barricades on a restricted road at the peak of a festival crowd.
